testimonials.quote: Every single detail felt considered. A private dinner on the ramparts of Galle Fort was the most romantic evening of our lives.

testimonials.name: Lukas Hoffmann
testimonials.quote: Our naturalist found us three leopards in one morning. The organisation was flawless: pünktlich, professional and warm.

testimonials.name: Amélie Laurent
testimonials.quote: Sigiriya at sunrise with nobody else around. Sasoba understood exactly the kind of journey I dreamed of.

testimonials.name: The Martinez Family
testimonials.quote: Our kids still talk about the whales and the tuk-tuk ride through Kandy. The 24/7 WhatsApp concierge was a lifesaver.

testimonials.name: Olivia Chen
testimonials.quote: I came home rested in a way I hadn’t felt in years. The Ayurveda retreat and tea-country train were pure magic.

destinations.name: Sigiriya
destinations.tagline: The Lion Rock fortress in the sky
destinations.intro: Rising 200 metres from the jungle, Sigiriya was the 5th-century palace of King Kashyapa. Climb past the famous cloud-maiden frescoes and the giant lion paws to the ruined summit palace, with the whole of the dry zone spread out below.

experiences.title: Private dawn ascent
experiences.text: Start at first light with a historian guide and have the summit almost to yourself.

experiences.title: Pidurangala sunset
experiences.text: Climb the neighbouring rock for the classic view of Sigiriya glowing at dusk.

experiences.title: Village & lake safari
experiences.text: Bullock cart, catamaran and a home-cooked rice-and-curry lunch in a farming village.

destinations.name: Dambulla Cave Temple
destinations.intro: Five cave shrines carved into a granite outcrop, filled with more than 150 Buddha statues and walls of vivid murals. Pilgrims have worshipped here for over two thousand years.

experiences.title: Early-morning visit
experiences.text: Arrive as the caves open, when the light is soft and the rock still cool.

experiences.title: Monk blessing
experiences.text: Receive a traditional pirith thread blessing from a resident monk.

experiences.title: Spice garden stop
experiences.text: Taste cinnamon, cardamom and pepper straight from the vine in nearby Matale.

destinations.name: Anuradhapura
destinations.tagline: The first great capital of Lanka
destinations.intro: For over a thousand years Anuradhapura ruled the island. Its colossal white dagobas, monastery ruins and the sacred Sri Maha Bodhi, grown from a cutting of the Buddha’s own Bodhi tree, make it the spiritual heart of Sri Lanka.

experiences.title: Ruins by bicycle
experiences.text: Cycle between monasteries and ancient reservoirs with an archaeologist.

experiences.title: Evening puja
experiences.text: Join white-clad pilgrims offering lotus flowers at sunset.

experiences.title: Mihintale climb
experiences.text: Climb to the hilltop where Buddhism first arrived on the island.

destinations.name: Polonnaruwa
destinations.tagline: A medieval royal city among the trees
destinations.intro: The island’s second capital is one of the best-preserved ancient cities in Asia. Royal palaces, lotus baths and the serene rock-carved Buddhas of Gal Vihara sit beside the vast Parakrama Samudra reservoir.

experiences.title: Cycle the ancient city
experiences.text: The flat, shaded site is perfect to explore by bicycle.

experiences.title: Minneriya add-on
experiences.text: Combine with an afternoon elephant safari just 30 minutes away.

experiences.title: Lakeside sunset
experiences.text: Watch fishermen return across the 12th-century reservoir.

destinations.name: Kandy
destinations.intro: Set around a lake in the green hills, Kandy was the seat of the last Sinhalese kings. The Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic is the most revered shrine in the country, and each July or August the city hosts the spectacular Esala Perahera.
highlights: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic

experiences.title: Evening puja at the Temple
experiences.text: Drums, incense and the opening of the relic chamber doors.

experiences.title: Kandyan dance
experiences.text: Fire-walking and whirling dancers in traditional dress.

experiences.title: Tea & spice trail
experiences.text: Visit a working tea factory and spice garden in the hills.

destinations.name: Nuwara Eliya
destinations.intro: At 1,900 metres, Nuwara Eliya is cool, misty and wrapped in emerald tea estates. Colonial bungalows, a Tudor-style post office and a lakeside racecourse recall its days as a British hill station.

experiences.title: Pluck with the pluckers
experiences.text: Join an estate team at dawn, then taste your own leaf.

experiences.title: Planter’s bungalow stay
experiences.text: Butlers, fireplaces and high tea in a restored estate home.

experiences.title: Scenic train
experiences.text: Ride one of the world’s most beautiful railways onward to Ella.

destinations.name: Ella
destinations.tagline: Rail bridges, peaks and valley views
destinations.intro: A laid-back village in a deep gap in the hills, Ella is the place for easy hikes and big views. Watch the blue train glide over the colonial Nine Arch Bridge, then hike Little Adam’s Peak for sunrise over the Ella Gap.

experiences.title: Kandy–Ella train
experiences.text: Reserved seats on the famous seven-hour ride through tea country.

experiences.title: Sunrise hike
experiences.text: Little Adam’s Peak at first light with a local guide.

experiences.title: Ayurvedic cooking class
experiences.text: Learn curry and sambol with a village family.

destinations.name: Horton Plains
destinations.intro: A high, windswept plateau of grassland and cloud forest, part of the Central Highlands World Heritage Site. A 9 km loop leads to World’s End, where the land drops almost 900 metres to the plains below.

experiences.title: Dawn trek
experiences.text: Reach World’s End before the mist rolls in, usually by 10am.

experiences.title: Birding walk
experiences.text: Look for endemic whistling thrush and dull-blue flycatcher.

experiences.title: Picnic breakfast
experiences.text: A hot hamper breakfast at the park gate after the hike.

destinations.name: Adam’s Peak (Sri Pada)
destinations.tagline: A night pilgrimage to a sacred summit
destinations.intro: Revered by Buddhists, Hindus, Muslims and Christians alike, this 2,243 m peak bears a “sacred footprint” at its summit. Pilgrims climb 5,500 lamp-lit steps through the night to watch the sunrise and the peak’s triangular shadow.

experiences.title: Guided night climb
experiences.text: Start around 2am with a guide, tea stops and warm layers.

experiences.title: Recovery massage
experiences.text: An Ayurvedic leg massage at your hill lodge afterwards.

experiences.title: Estate lodge
experiences.text: Rest in a tea-estate bungalow at the foot of the mountain.

destinations.name: Knuckles Range
destinations.tagline: Wild trekking off the beaten path
destinations.intro: Named for peaks that look like a clenched fist, the Knuckles range is a UNESCO-listed wilderness of cloud forest, waterfalls and remote villages: the island’s best multi-day trekking.

experiences.title: Two-day trek
experiences.text: Hike between villages with a porter team and a naturalist.

experiences.title: Eco-lodge nights
experiences.text: Sleep in a remote lodge with river views.

experiences.title: Village kitchen
experiences.text: Cook over a wood fire with a farming family.

destinations.name: Yala National Park
destinations.intro: Sri Lanka’s most famous park has one of the highest leopard densities in the world. Scrub jungle, lagoons and rocky outcrops also shelter elephants, sloth bears, crocodiles and more than 200 bird species.

experiences.title: Private 4×4 safaris
experiences.text: Morning and afternoon drives with a dedicated naturalist.

experiences.title: Luxury tented camp
experiences.text: Fall asleep to jungle sounds on the edge of the park.

experiences.title: Bush breakfast
experiences.text: A cooked breakfast set up in the wild between drives.

destinations.note: Block 1 usually closes for part of September–October.

destinations.name: Udawalawe
destinations.intro: Open grassland around a large reservoir makes Udawalawe the best place in Sri Lanka to watch wild elephants. Herds of several hundred live here year-round. The nearby Elephant Transit Home cares for orphaned calves before returning them to the wild.

experiences.title: Afternoon safari
experiences.text: Golden light over the reservoir as herds come to drink.

experiences.title: Transit Home visit
experiences.text: Watch orphaned calves at feeding time.

experiences.title: Stop en route
experiences.text: Perfect halfway break between the hills and the south coast.

destinations.name: Wilpattu National Park
destinations.intro: Sri Lanka’s largest national park is dotted with natural lakes called villus. Far fewer jeeps than Yala make Wilpattu a peaceful place to look for leopards, sloth bears and elephants.

experiences.title: Full-day safari
experiences.text: Picnic lunch inside the park to reach the remote west.

experiences.title: Eco-lodge stay
experiences.text: Solar-powered cabins on the park boundary.

experiences.title: Kalpitiya combo
experiences.text: Pair with dolphins and kitesurfing on the coast.

destinations.name: Minneriya
destinations.intro: In the dry season hundreds of elephants gather on the grassy shores of the ancient Minneriya reservoir, one of the largest meetings of Asian elephants on Earth.

experiences.title: Sunset jeep safari
experiences.text: The herds are most active in the late afternoon.

experiences.title: Kaudulla alternative
experiences.text: Your naturalist chooses the park where herds are that day.

experiences.title: Hurulu eco-park
experiences.text: A quieter option early in the year.

destinations.name: Sinharaja Rainforest
destinations.intro: A UNESCO-listed lowland rainforest where most of the trees and many of the birds are found nowhere else on Earth. Mixed-species bird flocks, purple-faced langurs and giant squirrels move through the canopy.

experiences.title: Guided rainforest walk
experiences.text: Walk with a village-born forest guide and a birder.

experiences.title: Canopy lodge
experiences.text: Stay in an eco-lodge right on the forest edge.

experiences.title: Night walk
experiences.text: Look for frogs, lizards and glowing fungi after dark.

destinations.name: Galle Fort
destinations.tagline: A living colonial fortress by the sea
destinations.intro: Built by the Portuguese and fortified by the Dutch, Galle Fort is a walled town of cobbled lanes, whitewashed churches, boutique hotels and galleries, and one of the best places on the coast to watch the sunset from the ramparts.

experiences.title: Heritage walk
experiences.text: Stories of spice traders and sea captains with a local historian.

experiences.title: Rampart dinner
experiences.text: A private candle-lit table on the fort walls.

experiences.title: Stilt fishermen
experiences.text: See the traditional fishermen at Koggala nearby.

destinations.name: Mirissa
destinations.intro: A crescent of golden sand famous for whale watching: blue whales and sperm whales pass close to the coast in season. After the boat, relax at Coconut Tree Hill or Secret Beach.

experiences.title: Responsible whale cruise
experiences.text: A small vessel with a marine biologist on board.

experiences.title: Surf lesson
experiences.text: Gentle beach breaks at nearby Weligama.

experiences.title: Clifftop villa
experiences.text: Private pool villa overlooking the bay.

destinations.name: Tangalle
destinations.intro: Long, empty beaches and rocky coves make Tangalle the south coast’s quiet hideaway. Nearby Rekawa is an important nesting beach for sea turtles, and Mulkirigala rock temple rises inland.

experiences.title: Turtle night watch
experiences.text: Watch nesting green turtles with a conservation project.

experiences.title: Beach-villa stay
experiences.text: A secluded villa with your own chef.

experiences.title: Hiriketiya day
experiences.text: Surf and cafés in the famous horseshoe bay.

destinations.name: Bentota
destinations.intro: Where the Bentota River meets the sea, this resort coast offers golden beaches, water sports and mangrove boat safaris, and it’s home to the gardens of Sri Lanka’s great architect, Geoffrey Bawa.

experiences.title: River safari
experiences.text: Look for monitor lizards and kingfishers in the mangroves.

experiences.title: Bawa garden tour
experiences.text: Explore the architect’s country estate, Lunuganga.

experiences.title: Ayurveda retreat
experiences.text: Traditional treatments at a beachfront spa.

destinations.name: Trincomalee
destinations.tagline: Deep harbour, white sand, blue whales
destinations.intro: One of the world’s finest natural harbours, with the white-sand beaches of Nilaveli and Uppuveli to the north. Snorkel with reef sharks at Pigeon Island and visit the clifftop Koneswaram Hindu temple.

experiences.title: Pigeon Island trip
experiences.text: Snorkel with turtles and blacktip reef sharks.

experiences.title: Whale cruise
experiences.text: Blue whales pass close to the east coast in season.

experiences.title: Temple at dusk
experiences.text: Evening puja at Koneswaram on Swami Rock.

destinations.name: Pasikudah
destinations.intro: A long, shallow bay protected by a reef, where you can wade far out into warm, calm water. Pasikudah is ideal for families and for a slow few days by the sea in summer.

experiences.title: Lazy beach days
experiences.text: Stay in a beachfront resort with a pool and spa.

experiences.title: Lagoon canoe
experiences.text: Paddle past fishing villages at sunrise.

experiences.title: Batticaloa trip
experiences.text: Visit the Dutch fort and the famous “singing fish” lagoon.

destinations.name: Arugam Bay
destinations.intro: A world-famous right-hand point break and a relaxed surf-village atmosphere. Between sessions, spot elephants at Kumana and Lahugala or watch crocodiles in the lagoons.

experiences.title: Surf coaching
experiences.text: Lessons for beginners, guided trips for experts.

experiences.title: Lagoon safari
experiences.text: Canoe through mangroves at dawn.

experiences.title: Kumana jeep safari
experiences.text: A wild, remote park with leopards and waterbirds.

destinations.name: Jaffna
destinations.tagline: Tamil culture in the far north
destinations.intro: Jaffna has its own distinct Tamil culture: grand Hindu kovils, a star-shaped Dutch fort, palmyra-palm landscapes and the island’s spiciest crab curry. Causeways lead out to quiet islands like Nainativu.

experiences.title: Kovil at puja time
experiences.text: Visit Nallur as the bells ring and lamps are lit.

experiences.title: Island hopping
experiences.text: Ferry to Nainativu for its Hindu and Buddhist shrines.

experiences.title: Food trail
experiences.text: Crab curry, odiyal kool and palmyra sweets.

destinations.name: Kalpitiya
destinations.intro: A long, windswept peninsula between lagoon and sea. Huge pods of spinner dolphins appear offshore in winter, while strong summer winds make it one of Asia’s top kitesurfing spots.

experiences.title: Dolphin cruise
experiences.text: Sometimes hundreds of spinner dolphins at once.

experiences.title: Kite school
experiences.text: Beginner courses on the flat-water lagoon.

experiences.title: Cabana stay
experiences.text: Barefoot beach eco-cabanas.

destinations.name: Colombo
destinations.intro: Sri Lanka’s buzzing commercial capital mixes colonial buildings, markets, temples and a fast-growing skyline. Stroll Galle Face Green at sunset, shop for design, and eat very well.

experiences.title: Tuk-tuk city tour
experiences.text: Markets, mosques, temples and colonial streets.

experiences.title: Street-food evening
experiences.text: Kottu, hoppers and isso wade at Galle Face.

experiences.title: Bawa architecture
experiences.text: Visit Number 11, Geoffrey Bawa’s home.

story: In Sri Lanka the peacock (monara) is a symbol of grace, pride and beauty. Its feathers carry every colour of our island: the teal of the ocean, the green of the tea hills, the gold of temple roofs and the orange of a south-coast sunset.
Sasoba was founded on the same idea. Every journey should unfold like a peacock’s fan: layered, colourful and full of moments that make you stop and stare.

values.title: Genuine hospitality
values.text: Sri Lankans say “Ayubowan”, meaning “may you live long”. We treat every traveller as a guest in our home.

values.title: Truly tailor-made
values.text: No fixed departures, no group coaches. Every day is planned around you.

values.title: Travel that gives back
values.text: Community-run experiences, carbon offsetting and conservation partners.

values.title: Licensed & safe
values.text: SLTDA-licensed guides, insured vehicles and 24/7 support.

etiquette: Cover shoulders and knees at temples; remove shoes and hats before entering.
Never pose with your back to a Buddha statue, and don’t touch statues.
Walk clockwise around stupas and bodhi trees.
Give and receive with your right hand.
Ask before photographing people, monks or ceremonies.
Clothing or tattoos showing the Buddha can cause serious offence.
